title: Jeremiah Stays with Gedaliah

questions.question: Where did Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let Jeremiah go from, after finding him bound in chains among all the captives?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:1 (ESV): "The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard had let him go from Ramah, when he took him bound in chains along with all the captives..."

questions.question: The captain of the guard acknowledged the theological reason for Jerusalem's fall to Jeremiah. What did he say?
options: "The Lord your God pronounced this disaster against this place... because you sinned against the Lord and did not obey his voice."
"Your army was too weak and your walls too thin."
"It is the fate of all who oppose the mighty king of Babylon."
"The gods of Babylon are stronger than your God."
questions.correctAnswer: "The Lord your God pronounced this disaster against this place... because you sinned against the Lord and did not obey his voice."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:2-3 (ESV): "The Lord your God pronounced this disaster against this place. The Lord has brought it about... because you sinned against the Lord and did not obey his voice..."

questions.question: The captain of the guard loosed Jeremiah's chains and told him he could come to Babylon or stay in the land. Which option did Jeremiah choose?
options: He stayed in the land of Judah
He went to Ramah to live alone
questions.correctAnswer: He stayed in the land of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5-6 (ESV): "Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah, and lived with him among the people who were left in the land."

questions.question: Who had the king of Babylon appointed governor in the land?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 (ESV): "Go back to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed governor of the cities of Judah,"

questions.question: Where did Gedaliah reside as governor?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:6 (ESV): "Then Jeremiah went to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, at Mizpah,"

questions.question: What did the captain of the guard give Jeremiah when he let him go?
options: An allowance of food and a present
questions.correctAnswer: An allowance of food and a present
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:5 (ESV): "So the captain of the guard gave him an allowance of food and a present, and let him go."

questions.question: When the captains of the forces in the open country heard that Gedaliah had been appointed governor over the poorest of the land, what did they do?
options: They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
questions.correctAnswer: They came to Gedaliah at Mizpah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:7-8 (ESV): "they came with their men to Gedaliah at Mizpah..."

questions.question: What did Gedaliah swear to the captains and their men when they arrived?
options: "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you."
"We will rebel when the time is right."
"You must hand your weapons over to me."
questions.correctAnswer: "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:9 (ESV): "Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, swore to them and their men, saying, 'Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it shall be well with you.'"

questions.question: What goods did Gedaliah instruct the people to gather and store in their vessels?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:10 (ESV): "but you, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and store them in your vessels, and dwell in your cities that you have taken."

questions.question: Judeans who had scattered to Moab, Ammon, Edom, and all the lands heard that a remnant was left in Judah under Gedaliah. What did they do?
options: They returned from all the places to which they had been driven and came to the land of Judah
They decided to stay where they were
They sent envoys to surrender to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: They returned from all the places to which they had been driven and came to the land of Judah
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:12 (ESV): "then all the Judeans returned from all the places to which they had been driven and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah."

questions.question: What did the returning Judeans gather in great abundance?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:12 (ESV): "And they gathered wine and summer fruits in great abundance."

questions.question: Who came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him of an assassination plot against him?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:13-14 (ESV): "Now Johanan the son of Kareah and all the leaders of the forces in the open country came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and said to him..."

questions.question: Who did Johanan say had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to take Gedaliah's life?
options: Baalis the king of the Ammonites
questions.correctAnswer: Baalis the king of the Ammonites
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:14 (ESV): "Do you know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to take your life?"

questions.question: What did Johanan the son of Kareah offer to do secretly for Gedaliah?
options: "Let me go and strike down Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it."
"Let me hire guards to protect you day and night."
"Let me send a message to Babylon for reinforcements."
"Let me take you to Egypt where you will be safe."
questions.correctAnswer: "Let me go and strike down Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it."
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:15 (ESV): "Then Johanan the son of Kareah spoke secretly to Gedaliah at Mizpah, 'Let me go and strike down Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no one will know it.'"

questions.question: Did Gedaliah believe Johanan that Ishmael was plotting to kill him?
options: No, he said Johanan was speaking falsely
Yes, he told Johanan to kill Ishmael
He was unsure and asked Jeremiah to pray
Yes, and he fled to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: No, he said Johanan was speaking falsely
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 40:16 (ESV): "But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said to Johanan the son of Kareah, 'You shall not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely of Ishmael.'"

key_verse_text: "And now, behold, I release you today from the chains on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will look after you well; but if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, do not come. See, the whole land is before you; go wherever you think it good and right to go."
